title: Delta sync: cursors, timestamps, and the clock that is wrong

videos.script:
So far the planner sent its changes up. Now the other direction. {{down}} What another phone wrote, brought down to this one.

The first version asks for everything. {{bytes}} Two hundred kilobytes, to learn that nothing changed. The cost follows the size of the data, and the data only grows.

So the device keeps a bookmark. {{cursor}} The server numbers every write, and the device asks for what came after its number. Nothing new costs twenty-eight bytes.

Why not a time instead? {{clock}} Because a phone's clock can be ten minutes slow, and a session stamped in the past is never seen again. And one more thing a delta needs. {{tombstone}} A delete has to leave a mark, or no question can find it.
